evidence: both variants report the size they declared, as the API sees it
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P11). The exact client build was not recorded at the time; attributed to the pack's declared floor. Re-run to replace with a real measurement.

evidence: Interacting does nothing
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P11). chest5 does not open; horse5 does, with every other component identical — same private:false, same is_chested, same size, generated from one template with only container_type substituted. So container_type is the whole difference, and is_chested alone is not sufficient.

evidence: A real container screen opens
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P11). A real container screen, titled from the entity's nameTag.

evidence: It draws the entity, and it turns to follow the cursor
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P11). The vanilla mob-preview behaviour, inherited for nothing — a free piece of identity on a screen that would otherwise need a title to carry it.

evidence: At least one draws a different count than it declared, but you could not open enough variants to say which rule applies
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P11). horse5 declares 5 and draws 3. horse1 and horse15 were added to bracket it and have not been read — so whether 3 is a CEILING or the layout is FIXED is still open, and those are different designs. Two slots the player can never reach and script can write to freely: a hazard if you assumed the screen shows what you stored, a primitive if you wanted storage a player cannot touch.

evidence: The diamond is there
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P11).

evidence: Any item goes in any slot and stays
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P11). This was the thing most likely to sink the route — a horse screen's slots are normally typed, and a container inheriting that would be useless for arbitrary items.

evidence: both variants spawn, carry a container, and script can read and write their slots
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P11), from a headless smoke job. The first run of this probe reported LocationInUnloadedChunkError for both variants — that was a defect in the probe, not a finding, and the fix was claiming a ticking area first.

evidence: 6 sightings across one 12-tick fall, with position AND velocity readable every tick
note: Imported from composable-portals (cportals:ritual drop). The velocities are vanilla falling-block gravity, which confirms the entity being watched is the real one rather than a look-alike, and that getVelocity() on it is not zeroed the way a collided entity's is.

evidence: The fetch works from wherever you are standing
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P12), reported from play: "The chunk unload seemed to work for the stash of the gun". This is the leg most likely to have killed the holder-per-item design outright.

evidence: It comes back as itself, but state the script API cannot read was not checked
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P12), reported from play: "The fetch works, I used it on a gun that definitely has metadata in it, so it seems to be fine." A gun carrying dynamic properties is a weaker witness than a filled shulker box — a codec could have carried the first and provably cannot carry the second.

evidence: setEquipment succeeded and the slot read back correctly
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P9).

evidence: a custom item declaring allow_off_hand was still in the slot on a later run
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P9), and observed incidentally rather than measured deliberately: the probe skipped itself because the off-hand already held one of our own items. That is weaker evidence than a designed trial, which is why bedshock's own offhand probe runs both arms explicitly.

evidence: read back correctly, and three seconds later the diamond was gone — the client ejects items the slot would not accept
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P9). Closes an attractive idea: had script-placed items stuck, the off-hand would have given free in-world rendering of an arbitrary item with no attachable work at all.

evidence: all six variants exist as real items, so whatever the menu does with them is hiding or showing, never rejecting
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P7), from a headless smoke job. Retires half of a standing warning: a custom group string does not cause rejection.

evidence: the token came back off the picked-up copy
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P8).

evidence: survives setItem then getItem — mutate-in-place is safe
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P8). Confirmed both on the smoke job and in-game through slot 9. The consequence is large: a state toggle need never swap item types, so the class of fault where a toggle silently drops stack data does not arise.

evidence: only one of the two spellings was ever looked at, and it was frozen
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P10). The first spelling (explicit frames, blend_frames false) came back frozen on frame 0. A single frozen icon cannot distinguish "item atlas tiles do not flipbook" from "this entry is wrong", which is why a second deliberately different spelling was added and has not been read. Recorded as inconclusive rather than as a leaning-no, because the ledger has no verdict for a hunch.

evidence: damage reached max-1 on every in-range ceiling
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P1), headless smoke job. damage == max_durability still means broken, so the usable top is max-1.

evidence: everything up to and including 32767 reports back exactly what was declared
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P1), headless smoke job, PR #36 run 30516360479. Vanilla's own ceiling is 2031 (netherite), so everything above that was undocumented territory. 15 usable bits.

evidence: two's-complement int16 wraparound, and the item still loads
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P1). A clamp has a safe failure mode and a wrap does not: an over-large value does not degrade to the maximum, it becomes negative and nonsensical, and the item still loads. Whatever computes a packed code must assert its own range.

evidence: The centres read as background — the holes are holes
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P5).

evidence: all four rings rendered in chat as red, green, blue and white
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P5). Vanilla's own pages being near-monochrome turns out to be a choice, not a limit. Read in CHAT only — whether the same glyph renders in an item name or the actionbar is a separate row and still open, and a glyph that works in chat and not on an item would be a trap.

evidence: geometry placed at the anchor is occluded by the player, in both first and third person
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P3a, then again on the P3b rig). Twice a rig rendered perfectly and could not be read for this reason. Offset a probe before measuring with it.

evidence: third person showed it plainly as a cube; first person was filled with magenta because the hand pivot is essentially at the camera
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P3a). The most consequential row in the battery was the negative, and it did not happen. The failure that would have killed the route was INVISIBLE — magenta everywhere is not invisible, and Bedrock's own missing-texture is a checker rather than a solid field, so the two were distinguishable.

evidence: two items differing only in damage (5 and 6) drew identically, with the control bone BLUE on both
note: Imported from composable-portals docs/CAPABILITIES.md (P3b/P4). Read differentially after two earlier attempts could not be graded: an absolute reading was structurally ambiguous, because with max_durability 2048 an undamaged item shows the same colours as a blind query. All three durability queries resolve to 0 — the expression resolves, it just never sees an item. Consequence: a render controller cannot be told which item it is drawing, so every distinguishable configuration needs its own item type, and per-stack state has to live in the NAME and the DURABILITY BAR.
